what: The public record of the cloud branch (docs/analysis_plan_models.md, Amendment 3, section 12). code_commit, code_published_at, code_published_source and the gist fields are filled after the branch's code commit is published, and key_reading (the output of `python -m judge.cloud --status`: the branch key's limit, its reset and the free daily limit) when the branch is registered, all before any request (Amendment 3, Correction, C1 and C10); the runner refuses while any is null. Times are GitHub's, not the author's clock. Amendment 3, Correction 5, C26: the owner waived a credit limit on the branch key on 2026-11-12 (key_limit_waived, key_limit_waiver: his words in Russian and in English). A key that has a limit must still have exactly 15 USD that never resets; on a key without a limit the paid arm runs only under this waiver and only on a reading of the account's credit balance that the operator takes by hand from the OpenRouter dashboard before each paid run and appends to account_balance_readings ({"balance_usd", "read_at" in UTC with its offset, "read_by", "source", and, by Correction 6, C28, "auto_top_up": false}); the code cannot read the balance (GET /api/v1/credits needs a management key) and checks only the reading's form, time and size. Under the waiver the bound is the code's caps. Amendment 3, Correction 6, C28 (which overrides Correction 5's "the only outer bound the account's balance"): the balance is an outer bound only while the account's auto top-up is off, so each reading also records "auto_top_up": false (exactly false, read on the Credits page), and the runner refuses a reading without it; even then the bound is the balance as read, not a fixed 25 USD (it can be topped up by hand), and OpenRouter may let it go below zero by about one request. A reading is accepted only if it is not ahead of the runner's clock and later than the reading of every earlier paid run under the waiver (one reading, one paid run); key_reading's usage is the baseline from which the key's use is compared with the spend journal.
code_published_source: GitHub repository activity API (repos/dmitri-sulga/refund-decision-eval/activity): push of main from 60dfe9b to ffcc1e5 (nine commits, a192234..ffcc1e5, published through the git-data API with their local SHAs, non-forced update of main)
gist_visibility: secret (unlisted: anyone with the link can read it)
gist_content: the commit id above and the SHA-256 of 140 files at that commit: the 18 protected files of src/judge/cloud.py (PROTECTED: the plan with Amendment 3 and its Corrections, the branch's runner, selection, analysis and tests, the earlier runners, the frozen prompt, request, parsing, metric, data and label code, and the Makefile), pre_run_checklist.md, this file as committed with the publication fields empty, and each of the 120 snapshot files, then the snapshot's combined hash (snapshot_sha256 above)

key_reading.read_with: python -m judge.cloud --status (GET /api/v1/key with the branch key; no model called, nothing billed; the key's label is not kept)
key_reading.auto_top_up_source: not part of GET /api/v1/key: read on the OpenRouter dashboard's Credits page by the coordinator on 2026-11-12 at about 17:54 UTC (the Auto Top-Up block offers "Enable"; nothing was changed)

key_limit_waiver.quote_ru: это лимит никакой, там и так 25 долларов, просто работаю аккуратно и все нормально делают
key_limit_waiver.quote_en: this limit is pointless; there are only 25 dollars there anyway; I just work carefully, and everyone does it normally
key_limit_waiver.meaning: the account holds a 25 USD balance; he declines a credit limit on the key and accepts working carefully without one
key_limit_waiver.given_by: the author, owner of the OpenRouter account, in a chat message to his AI coding assistant
key_limit_waiver.what_it_weakens: no stop outside the code at 15 USD: the code's caps (15 USD branch, 5 USD per model, each request reserved at its worst case, the spend journal) are the bound; a defect in them could in principle exceed 15 USD; outside the code only the account's balance bounds it, and only while auto top-up is off (Amendment 3, Correction 6, C28, overriding "the only outer bound"): the balance as read before each paid run, not a fixed 25 USD, which OpenRouter may let go below zero by about one request
